fatal_errors: The proposed h-BN addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which varied Mo content in an existing CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
The baseline is incorrectly treated as unmodified CoCrFeNi rather than the Mo0.2 self-lubricating composite.
The claim that an h-BN tribofilm will persist in air through 800 °C is unsupported and overlooks oxidation and tribochemical changes at high temperature.
The prediction of coefficient of friction below 0.3 and more than 50% wear reduction at every temperature is unsupported and ignores the severe 200–400 °C performance regime.
No cited evidence supports h-BN compatibility, processing feasibility, phase stability, or tribofilm continuity in this matrix.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of wide-temperature self-lubrication and proposes a controlled comparison with measurable friction, wear, and surface chemistry. However, it is a different and insufficiently supported intervention. It omits the target composite constituents, Mo-dependent FCC lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, low-temperature MoS2/Ag lubrication, and high-temperature NiO/silver-molybdate glaze formation. Test conditions are only loosely specified and differ from the target's ball-on-disk test at 8 N, 0.15 m/s, and 270 m against Si3N4. Its falsification experiment is directionally useful, but the rule demanding simultaneous improvement at every temperature conflates failure of an overstrong performance threshold with failure of the proposed mechanism. Without evidence for h-BN survival and continuous transfer-film formation in air at 800 °C, the proposal remains unsupported rather than a well-supported plausible alternative.
